title: Punctual cohomological purity over a prime field
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

Let $k$ be a prime field, meaning $\mathbf Q$ or $\mathbf F_p$ for a prime $p$. Every regular Noetherian $k$-scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible is punctually pure. No finite-type or excellence hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.2.5, printed p.245 (citing Fujiwara 2002, Corollary 2.2.3). Only the statement in ILO is used; no prohibited trace route is selected.

proof.text: Fix $w\in X$ and put $R=\mathcal O_{X,w}$, $d=\dim R$. Regularity and Noetherianity of $X$ mean that $R$ is Noetherian regular local; the structure map gives a prime-field subring of $R$, and $\ell$ remains invertible. Apply [lem-per-punctual-strict-completion-test] to $R$. It supplies $B=\widehat{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}$, Noetherian regular local, complete, strictly henselian and of dimension $d$, and says that punctual purity for $R$ at its closed point is equivalent to that for $B$. The composite from the prime field into $B$ is injective: it is a unital map from a field to the nonzero local ring $B$. Thus $B$ still contains that prime field.

source.place: XVI, Definitions 3.2.1–3.2.2, Proposition 3.2.4 and Proposition 3.2.5, printed pp.244–245; agent reconstruction of the prime-field proof using Cohen coordinates and regular supported base change.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-prime-field-complete-coordinate-model] to $B$. Write $F=B/\mathfrak m_B$, $C=F[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$, $I=(T_1,\ldots,T_d)$ and identify $\widehat C_I$ with $B$ by its coordinate-preserving isomorphism. Put $P=\mathbf A^d_F=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}F$, let $p:P\to S$ be the projection and $z:S\hookrightarrow P$ the zero section. The inverse image of $z$ under $h:\operatorname{Spec}B\to P$ is exactly the closed point $j:S\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$: the affine fibre-product formula gives its ring $B\otimes_C C/I=B/IB=B/\mathfrak m_B=F$, with induced map on $S$ the identity. Invertibility of $\ell$ in $B$ implies invertibility in $F$ and hence in $C$.

source.place: XVI, Definitions 3.2.1–3.2.2, Proposition 3.2.4 and Proposition 3.2.5, printed pp.244–245; agent reconstruction of the prime-field proof using Cohen coordinates and regular supported base change.

proof.text: The field $F$ is excellent by [lem-exc-fields-excellent]. The polynomial algebra $C$ is of finite type over $F$, so [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] makes $C$ excellent. By the definition of excellence it is Noetherian and a G-ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular] at the ideal $I$: $C\to\widehat C_I=B$ is flat and has geometrically regular Noetherian fibres. The flat affine criterion and affine fibre-product formula show that $h:\operatorname{Spec}B\to P$ is a regular morphism of Noetherian schemes. The fibre criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] verifies that these fibres stay regular under every finite residue-field extension, as required by [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change]. This argument uses excellence only for $C$, never for $R$.

source.place: XVI, Definitions 3.2.1–3.2.2, Proposition 3.2.4 and Proposition 3.2.5, printed pp.244–245; agent reconstruction of the prime-field proof using Cohen coordinates and regular supported base change.

proof.text: The projection $p$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. It is separated and compactifiable: the standard open immersion of affine space into projective space followed by the proper projective-space projection gives its compactification; the same is true of the closed section and their identity composite. Both $P$ and $S$ are Noetherian by Step 3 and the field case. The section is regular of codimension $d$ by [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus]. At coefficient level $n=1$, [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality] makes the shifted smooth orientation $a_p:A_P\to p^!A_S(-d)[-2d]$ an isomorphism. The section identity of [lem-per-smooth-gysin-mixed-identities] says $z^?(a_p)\circ a_z=1_{A_S}$, where $z^?=z^!(d)[2d]$ and $a_z:A_S\to z^!A_P(d)[2d]$ is the supported Kummer class. Since a functor preserves inverse identities, $z^?(a_p)$ is invertible. Multiplying the displayed identity by its inverse proves $a_z=(z^?(a_p))^{-1}$, so $a_z$ is an isomorphism with the specified Kummer normalization.

source.place: XVI, Definitions 3.2.1–3.2.2, Proposition 3.2.4 and Proposition 3.2.5, printed pp.244–245; agent reconstruction of the prime-field proof using Cohen coordinates and regular supported base change.

proof.text: For the closed immersions $z$ and $j$, the compactification $(1,z)$, resp. $(1,j)$, of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $Rz_!=z_*$ and $Rj_!=j_*$, so the compact-support right adjoints used by [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] and the closed-support adjoints $z_*\dashv z^!$, $j_*\dashv j^!$ of [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction] are right adjoints of the same functors; we identify them by the unique comparison of right adjoints compatible with the counits. Apply [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change] with $h$, $z$, and the constant coefficient object $A_P$, where $A=\mathbf Z/\ell=\mathbf F_\ell$. Step 2 identifies the closed fibre with $j$ and its map to $S$ with the identity. The theorem, including its twist and shift compatibility, therefore gives an isomorphism $z^!A_P(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}j^!A_B(d)[2d]$. By flat-base-change compatibility of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], the composite of $a_z$ with this exchange is precisely the Kummer fundamental-class map $a_j:A_F\to j^!A_B(d)[2d]$. The codimension is $d$ on both sides: $z$ has codimension $d$, and $B$ is regular local of dimension $d$. Thus $a_j$ is an isomorphism. This proves punctual purity of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ at its closed point.

source.place: XVI, Definitions 3.2.1–3.2.2, Proposition 3.2.4 and Proposition 3.2.5, printed pp.244–245; agent reconstruction of the prime-field proof using Cohen coordinates and regular supported base change.

proof.text: By the equivalence of Step 1, $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is punctually pure at its closed point. This is exactly punctual purity of $X$ at $w$. Since $w$ was arbitrary, $X$ is punctually pure. If $X$ is empty the assertion has no points to check. If $d=0$, all coordinate tuples are empty, $p=z=h=1_S$ under the coordinate model and all class maps above are the identity; no positive-dimension hypothesis entered the argument.
